scope: Tiny paired local contracts;root-owned runtime qualification is separate.

cases.title: Add an explicit tolerant parse column
cases.input_contract: Return all source columns plus parsed_amount from try_cast(trim(amount_text) AS BIGINT). Preserve eight rows and distinguish this nullable parse result from a final validity decision.
cases.expected: Ordered parsed values are 100,0,25, NULL, NULL, NULL,-5,50. The output parsed type is bigint.
cases.verification: Compare all eight(event_id, parsed_amount) pairs and the field type with literals.

cases.title: Classify missing versus rejected tokens
cases.input_contract: Add parse_status with missing for source NULL, rejected for a nonnull source that parsed to NULL, and valid otherwise. Keep all original rows and parsed values.
cases.expected: IDs 1,2,3,7,8 are valid, ID 4 missing, and IDs 5,6 rejected. Counts are 5,1,2 and sum to 8.
cases.verification: Assert the ordered status list and the exact two rejected IDs.

cases.title: Project the six parse-accepted events
cases.input_contract: Retain valid and missing statuses, then return event_id and parsed_amount aliased as amount_cents. Reject only malformed/overflowing nonnull tokens at this stage.
cases.expected: IDs[1,2,3,4,7,8] remain with amounts[100,0,25, NULL,-5,50]. There are 6 rows,5 known values and total 170.
cases.verification: Assert the exact rows and independent count/known/sum metrics.

cases.title: Express the same parse contract in SQL
cases.input_contract: Register the raw frame as a session-local view and produce the same six event_id, amount_cents rows using a SQL parse CTE and explicit missing-or-success filter. Compare with literals rather than only with the DataFrame result.
cases.expected: The SQL ordered rows are exactly the six rows from Exercise 3, including the NULL amount and signed-5.
cases.verification: Assert the SQL result against the full literal row list and separately compare the DataFrame path to that list.

cases.title: Observe strict ANSI failure at evaluation
cases.input_contract: Return a strict trimmed BIGINT cast projection. Evaluate a valid subset successfully, then intentionally evaluate the bad token at ID 5 under ANSI mode and require a CAST_INVALID_INPUT diagnostic. Do not count an unrelated exception as success.
cases.expected: The valid subset has the same six rows. ID 5 fails when collected, and the reference records the expected failure code before continuing.
cases.verification: Assert ANSI readback true, valid-row results, and a caught diagnostic containing CAST_INVALID_INPUT.

cases.title: Apply a separate nonnegative domain policy
cases.input_contract: From parse-accepted rows, retain unknown amounts and known nonnegative amounts. Return event_id, amount_cents and report the separate negative-domain rejection at ID 7 in the checks.
cases.expected: Final IDs[1,2,3,4,8] have 5 rows,4 known values, total 175. The full source reconciles as 5 final accepted+2 parse rejected+1 negative-domain rejected.
cases.verification: Assert final rows/metrics, negative ID 7 and the 8-row conservation equation.
